extracted.intended_audience: Australian publishers, editors, journalists, and media practitioners (and media complaints/adjudication stakeholders)
extracted.subtask_description: Adjudication applying the Australian Press Council's Standards of Practice to a news article, evaluating fairness/balance, relevance of personal characteristics, and whether publication caused or contributed to substantial prejudice or offence.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Principle 3: Ensure factual material is presented with reasonable fairness and balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications must take reasonable steps to ensure that factual material is presented with reasonable fairness and balance, and that writers’ expressions of opinion are not based on significantly inaccurate factual material or omission of key facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council accepts steps such as contacting subjects for comment and considers whether the article as a whole focused on the relevant comments. The adjudication found the publication had taken reasonable steps in this case (contacting the student, noting the opportunity to comment), and therefore complied with General Principle 3. Scoring note: assess whether reasonable pre-publication steps were taken and whether opinions rely on inaccurate facts or key omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Principle 6: Avoid causing or contributing materially to substantial offence, distress or prejudice (unless justified by sufficient public interest)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications must avoid causing or contributing materially to substantial offence, distress or prejudice, or a substantial risk to health or safety, unless doing so is sufficiently in the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where unnecessary emphasis on personal characteristics could lead readers to criticise views based on irrelevant attributes or contribute to prejudice, this Principle is engaged. The Council concluded that prominent reference to the student's gender identity and sexuality (when not relevant) could contribute to substantial prejudice and was not sufficiently justified by public interest, so the article breached General Principle 6. When harm is alleged, weigh whether inclusion is demonstrably in the public interest before publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance and prominence of personal characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications should not prominently report personal characteristics (eg. race, religion, nationality, country of origin, gender, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, illness or age) unless they are relevant to the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Council emphasises exercising great care not to place unwarranted emphasis on such characteristics. Example: prominently identifying a student as 'non-binary queer' when that status is not a reported reason for their views can lead readers to reject opinions on the basis of irrelevant personal characteristics and contribute to prejudice. Remove or avoid irrelevant identifying details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to take reasonable steps at time of publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications are obliged to take reasonable steps to comply with the Standards of Practice at the time of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-publication amendments (such as removing references or photographs) are welcomed as remedies but do not replace the obligation to take adequate care before publishing. Assessment should focus on the publisher's pre-publication processes and decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid gratuitous or salacious imagery and identifiers that contribute to prejudice
rubrics_metrics.description: Including photographs or salacious identifying details that serve no clear public-interest purpose may contribute to prejudice or salaciousness and should be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case the inclusion of several photographs attributed to the subject's Instagram and prominent references to sexual orientation/gender identity were considered to potentially contribute to prejudice; the Council welcomed the publisher's removal of these images and references. Guidance: evaluate whether images or attributions are necessary and proportionate to the public interest in publishing them.
